simple.meaning: עָקֹב (ʻâqôb) is a Hebrew word meaning “(transitive) fraudulent or (intransitive) tracked.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: עָקֹב (H6121) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Isaiah 40:4, with occurrences in Isaiah, Jeremiah, Hosea.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עָקֹב (H6121) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in עָקֹב (H6121) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: עָקֹב (ʻâqôb) / H6121 is traced through Isaiah 40:4, Jeremiah 17:9, Hosea 6:8 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H6121. aqob I. עָקֹב adjective 1 insidious, deceitful , Jer 17:9 מִכֹּל הַלֵּב עָקֹב . 2 foot-tracked (denominative from I. עָקֵב ) Hosea 6:8 מִדָּם עֲֹקֻבָּה אָוֶן מֹּעֲלֵי קִרְיַת גִּלְעָד . II. עָקֹב adjective steep, hilly (see √; compare difficult mountain path , Qor 90:11 hill ); — Isa 40:4 לְמִישׁוֺר הֶעָקֹב והיה let the steep ground (Chronicles) become a plain (|| הָֽרְכָסִים ). compare Ecclus 6:20.
definitions.rootNote: from 6117 ; in the original sense, a knoll (as swelling up); in the denominative sense
